checkpoint_kind: implemented feature delivery with pending browser validation
delivered: Independent original PNML and original event sources expose three exact public calls: decision mining, encoded decision tables, and guarded data Petri nets. Each request owns its source/model and invokes its declared native operation without reading or changing the cached mined session or synthesizing a miner identifier.

All native option structs retain 32 expanded option leaves: nine mining controls, twelve table controls including their independent nested mining options, and eleven guarded-net controls including nested decision options. Exact size_t tokens, IEEE doubles, negative zero, literal strings and ordered duplicate attribute lists survive; supplied-member provenance includes actual dotted nested paths. Native semantic validation owns its depth/lookback/gain/attribute constraints.

The encoded table outer include_trace_attributes default false remains distinct from nested mining default true. Outer attributes and nested mining attributes remain independent. Empty outer attribute names, missing optional feature cells, pre-choice context and bounded history retain their actual native behavior. No trimming, comma splitting, deduplication or cross-copying of the option scopes changes the request.

Complete results retain every stored decision counter, point, branch, flat node, child sentinel and inactive split field, plus ordered table classes/feature names/rows, exact targets and null/IEEE feature cells. Guarded outputs retain the full returned native net and a separate ordered guarded_transitions vector with full guard/read/write state. Disabling decision diagnostics clears native decision_points while preserving counters, tables, guards and the unchanged copied model.

Five PNML import controls preserve original document IDs, marking counts/keys, arcs and optional stochastic metadata. Decision APIs accept PetriNet and use native workflow boundaries; arbitrary PNML marking counts are provenance and are not injected as an invented replay policy. Original CSV/TSV/XES/gzip XES/typed-table sources retain all import controls, literal selectors, original/prepared views, full metadata, exact bytes and actual preparation errors. Binary source bytes use reversible hex transport.

The application provides independent model/source ownership and cancellation guards, all three operations, complete raw and named option editors, full inspection, exact original/source/request/raw/report/CSV/selected-record downloads and independently guarded source PNML/XES and structural result PNML exports. Learned guard expressions remain in the complete result; a structural PNML export does not evaluate them. Native suites, API captures, complete export verification, byte-identical portable fixtures and the final full frontend/production build support this delivery.

Shared multipart transport for Monte Carlo, playout and original-model decisions now sends CR/LF-bearing control values as exact byte file parts, alongside the existing lone-surrogate carrier. Actual Request serialization tests preserve literal import names and multiline options without browser FormData newline normalization. The native routes already accept these control file parts.
